claim: Abbaye de Charlieu admission is €5 full / €4 reduced with under-12 free, and a 4-site 'Explorez la Loire au fil des siècles' pass costs €12 covering the Couvent des Cordeliers and other departmental sites.
quote: Plein tarif : 5 € … Tarif réduit : 4 € … Gratuité : enfants de moins de 12 ans … Le pass annuel 'Explorez la Loire au fil des siècles' … Entrées illimitées pour les 4 sites

claim: Charlieu Abbey is open Monday and Wednesday–Sunday 10am–1pm and 2–6pm April–October (closed Tuesdays and 1 May), shorter 2–5pm afternoons February–March and November–December, and shut for January.
quote: April-October: Monday, Wednesday-Friday, weekends 10am-1pm, 2-6pm (closed May 1st) … February-March: Monday, Wednesday-Friday, weekends 10am-1pm, 2-5pm

claim: The abbey's must-see is its 12th-century Romanesque grand portal whose tympanum decoration draws on the Book of the Apocalypse, considered a masterpiece of Romanesque sculpture.
quote: The grand portal, whose decoration draws inspiration from the book of the Apocalypse, is a masterpiece of 12th-century Romanesque art.

claim: The Couvent des Cordeliers at Saint-Nizier-sous-Charlieu, just across the Sornin from the abbey, charges €5 full / €4 reduced (€8 with guided tour) at 1 Chemin des Cordeliers, 42190.
quote: Standard admission: €5 … Reduced rate: €4 … Admission with guided/thematic tour: €8 standard, €7 reduced … 1 Chemin des Cordeliers, 42190 Saint Nizier sous Charlieu

claim: The convent preserves one of the rare medieval Franciscan cloisters surviving in France, a Rayonnant Gothic ensemble whose north gallery is lined with figurative capitals.
quote: The cloister of the Cordeliers convent is one of the few medieval Franciscan cloisters still preserved in France. The grand cloister, in Rayonnant Gothic style, has very refined decoration, and its north gallery in particular is adorned with figurative capitals.

claim: The Prieuré d'Ambierle, a Cluniac flamboyant-Gothic church with original stained glass, is entered free of charge year-round, with guided tours organised by the Maison de Pays during summer.
quote: The church in flamboyant Gothic style houses period stained-glass windows and an altarpiece that is a masterpiece of Flemish art … accessible year-round and free of charge … the Maison de Pays d'Ambierle organizes guided tours

claim: The priory's centrepiece is the 5.60-metre Passion altarpiece, a Brussels polyptych of c. 1466 attributed to the workshop of Rogier van der Weyden or his successor, commissioned by Michel de Chaugy.
quote: This polyptych, which extends over 5.60m, comprises a central sculpted section retracing the Passion of Christ and shutters … The work bears a Brussels mark; various historical clues thus designate Brabant as the place of creation, around 1466, and probably the workshop of Roger Van der Weyden or his successor.

claim: Musée Alice Taverne in Ambierle, set in an 18th-c bourgeois house, recreates Roannais–Forez rural life 1850–1940 with workshops, a village dressmaker, country inn and 1940s daily-life rooms.
quote: The permanent exhibitions showcase rural life from the 1850s through WWII, featuring: Domestic scenes of peasant women … Village tradespeople's workshops, including a clockmaker and barrel maker … A recreated village dressmaker's shop and country inn

claim: The Alice Taverne museum is open 1 April–15 November 2026 — Tue–Fri 10–12 and 14–18 plus weekend afternoons in shoulder season, daily in July–August — and is closed entirely from mid-November to end of March.
quote: April 1–June 30 & September 1–November 15: Tuesday–Friday 10am–12pm, 2pm–6pm; Saturday–Sunday 2pm–6pm (closed Mondays); July 1–August 31: Daily 10am–12pm, 2pm–6pm

claim: Château de la Roche perches at 437 m on a rocky pinnacle above the Loire gorges at Saint-Priest-la-Roche, staging five 'show rooms' with theatrical scenography and seasonal escape games.
quote: Perched at 437 meters elevation … sits on 'a rocky peak since the 13th century' and 'overhangs the river' … 'five show rooms' that chronicle different historical periods through theatrical scenography

claim: Entry costs €8 full / €6 reduced with under-6s free; the castle runs daily in summer (9.30–12.30 and 14–19 from 6 July to 31 August 2026) and weekends-plus in shoulder months, closing in winter.
quote: From July 6 to August 31, 2026, it's open daily from 9:30 am to 12:30 pm and from 2 pm to 7 pm … Full price is €8, reduced price is €6 … free entry for children under 6

claim: The Musée Joseph Déchelette at 22 rue Anatole France in Roanne charges €5 full / €2.80 reduced with under-26s free, and offers free entry every Wednesday afternoon and on the first Sunday of each month.
quote: Full price: 5 € … Reduced rate: 2.80 € … Free for under 26s … Access to permanent collections is free on Wednesday afternoons and free for everyone on the first Sunday of each month.

claim: Housed in an 18th-c hôtel particulier with its garden, the Déchelette museum spans Prehistory to the 20th century with strong holdings in archaeology, Egyptian and East-Asian art, photography and one of France's richest provincial ceramics collections including 700 pieces of revolutionary earthenware.
quote: rich and varied course from Prehistory to the 20th century, open to extra-Western arts (Japan, China, Africa), Egyptian art, photography … one of the richest provincial ceramic collections (700 pieces of revolutionary earthenware, Sèvres porcelain, etc.)

claim: Château de Boisy in Pouilly-les-Nonains, just west of Roanne, is a 15th-c fortified manor bought in 1447 by royal treasurer Jacques Cœur; its square donjon and round towers are listed historic monuments (inscrit 1927, classé 1931).
quote: Jacques Cœur acquired it in 1447 … features a square donjon (keep) and round towers … inscription in 1927 for facades and roofs, classification in 1931 for exterior sections of south and east wings, southeast round tower and northeast square donjon
